# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 4, 2026
**Re:** Fubeix Thermal Distribution, LLC / Draisath Cooling Technologies, Inc.: review of distribution arrangements and recommended next steps
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Bottom line

Fubeix has five live problems under its arrangements with Draisath. Two are time-critical.

1. **Change of Control (urgent, before the December 2026 closing).** The Ostrava acquisition of Fubeix's parent needs Draisath's **prior written consent**, which Draisath can withhold in its sole discretion. The September 21 letter gives notice only and does not request consent. If closing happens without consent, Draisath can terminate immediately.
2. **Price objection (already lost).** Fubeix objected to the July 1, 2026 price increase on September 21, 2026. The 45-day window closed on August 15, 2026. The 9% CDU increase is **deemed accepted** and has applied since October 1, 2026. Any relief now has to be negotiated.
3. **Minimum purchase commitment (Contract Year 1 ends January 14, 2027).** The side letter lowered the commitment to $6,000,000. It also redefined "Products" as CDUs only, and the side letter prevails. RDHx and spare-parts purchases therefore no longer count toward the commitment.
4. **Non-compete (possible ongoing exposure).** Section 4.3 is worldwide and covers *all* thermal management products, with an 18-month tail. The term sheet agreed competing CDUs in the Territory only. This may already reach Fubeix's air-side cooling business. After closing, it may also reach the Ostrava group.
5. **Auto-renewal (diarize now; window opens October 2028).** The agreement renews for successive five-year terms unless notice is given in a 15-day window around October 1–16, 2028. The term sheet agreed one-year renewals by mutual agreement.

We recommend one coordinated approach to Draisath: a consent request covering items 1, 3, 4 and 5, plus a commercial ask on item 2. Draisath's consent is the main point of leverage on both sides, so it makes sense to handle these together.

---

## 2. Key facts and dates

| Item | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Effective Date | January 15, 2026 | Distribution Agreement (DA), Preamble |
| Initial Term | Three (3) years from the January 15, 2026 Effective Date, ending January 14, 2029 | DA §2.1 |
| Renewal | Automatic successive five (5) year terms; 15-day opt-out window ending 90 days before expiry | DA §2.2 |
| Territory | NY, NJ, PA, CT, MA | DA §1.1 |
| Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment | $8,000,000 in the DA, reduced to **$6,000,000 per Contract Year** from Contract Year 1 | DA §5.1; Side Letter §§2.1–2.2 |
| Contract Year 1 | January 15, 2026 – January 14, 2027 | DA §1.1; Side Letter §2.2 |
| Shortfall remedy | Within 90 days after the Contract Year ends, Draisath may convert to non-exclusive or terminate on 60 days' notice | DA §§5.3, 13.2 |
| Price Adjustment Notice | Dated July 1, 2026; +9% on all CDU list prices, effective October 1, 2026 | Letter §2.1 |
| Objection deadline | 45 days after notice date = **August 15, 2026** | DA §6.3 |
| Fubeix objection | September 21, 2026 (82 days after notice) | Letter §2.2 |
| Parent transaction | Ostrava Climate Holdings to acquire 100% of Fubeix Industrial Group, Inc.; closing expected December 2026 | Letter §1 |
| Order of precedence | Signed side letter, then DA, then Exhibits | DA §18.4 |
| Governing law / forum | New York; New York County courts | DA §§18.2–18.3 |

---

## 3. Issues

### Issue 1: Change of Control requires Draisath's prior written consent, and the letter does not request it

**Where:** DA §1.1 ("Change of Control"), §17.2, §13.3; Letter of September 21, 2026, §1 (esp. §1.4); Term Sheet §10.2.

**What the documents say:**
- Under DA §1.1, a "Change of Control" includes the acquisition of more than 50% of the voting interests of "any entity that directly or indirectly controls that Party." Ostrava's acquisition of all of Fubeix Industrial's equity falls squarely within this.
- DA §17.2 deems any Change of Control of Distributor, "including a change of control of any entity that directly or indirectly controls Distributor," to be an assignment. That assignment requires Draisath's **prior written consent, "which Supplier may grant or withhold in its sole discretion."** An assignment made in violation is void.
- DA §13.3 lets Draisath terminate **immediately by written notice** if a Change of Control occurs without its prior written consent.
- Letter §1.4 says the letter "satisfies any notice requirement under the Agreement" and that Fubeix will advise once closing occurs. It does not ask for consent.

**Why it matters:**
- The agreement does not run on notice. **Notice is not consent.** The letter's statement that notice requirements are satisfied is beside the point. Arguably it also signals to Draisath that Fubeix does not think consent is needed.
- Fubeix will remain a wholly owned subsidiary (Letter §1.3), but that does not help. The definition expressly captures changes at the parent level.
- If the deal closes without consent, Draisath gets a no-cure, immediate termination right. That would end Fubeix's exclusivity in the five-state Territory. Draisath could also use the threat of termination to reopen pricing, minimums or other terms.
- Because consent is in Draisath's sole discretion, there is no reasonableness standard for Fubeix to rely on.
- **Knock-on non-compete risk.** DA §4.3 bars Distributor from competing "directly or indirectly, through any Affiliate or otherwise." Once closing occurs, Ostrava and its group become Fubeix Affiliates (common control). If Ostrava or its portfolio companies make or distribute any third-party thermal management products anywhere in the world, Draisath could argue a §4.3 breach. That point is likely to come up in the consent discussion anyway.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Send a formal consent request now** under DA §18.1: hand or overnight courier, or email with a courier copy, addressed to Draisath's General Counsel. The request should expressly reference §17.2 and §13.3 and ask for written consent to the Transaction before closing. It should also clarify that Letter §1.4 is not intended to be the operative compliance step.
2. **Coordinate with the client's M&A counsel.** Draisath's consent should be treated as a required third-party consent. Ideally it should be a closing condition, or at least a covenant with a disclosure-schedule item. We should also confirm how the acquisition agreement allocates the risk of a refusal.
3. **Ask Draisath for a written consent that also covers the issues below.** At a minimum, the consent should confirm that the Ostrava group's activities do not breach §4.3, and ideally it should narrow §4.3 itself (Issue 4).
4. **Do not let the deal close** until consent is received or the client makes an informed decision to accept the termination risk.

---

### Issue 2: The objection to the July 1, 2026 price increase was untimely; the increase is deemed accepted

**Where:** DA §6.2, §6.3, §18.5; Letter of September 21, 2026, §2 (esp. §§2.2, 2.4); Term Sheet §6.3.

**What the documents say:**
- Under DA §6.3, Distributor may object "within 45 days after the date of a Price Adjustment Notice." If no timely written objection is made, Distributor "is deemed to have accepted the adjustment." The prior-price standstill and 30-day good-faith negotiation apply only "[i]f Distributor objects in time."
- The notice is dated July 1, 2026, so the period expired on **August 15, 2026**. The clock runs from the *date of* the notice, not its receipt.
- Letter §2.2 ("Distributor hereby objects to the price increase") is dated September 21, 2026, which is 82 days after the notice and 37 days late.
- On its face the notice appears to comply with DA §6.2. It gave more than 90 days' lead time (July 1 to October 1) and identified the products, the increase and the effective date. We should still check the notice itself.

**Why it matters:**
- The 9% CDU increase is **deemed accepted** and applies to all Purchase Orders accepted on or after October 1, 2026. The September 21 letter does not preserve Fubeix's rights, and its general reservation in §3.2 does not change that.
- The letter's statement in §2.4 that Fubeix "expects" invoicing at the old prices has no contractual basis. If Fubeix short-pays invoices on that basis:
  - the withheld amounts are unlikely to qualify as good-faith "disputed" amounts under §6.4;
  - they would accrue interest at up to 1% per month under §6.5; and
  - they could found a material-breach termination after a 30-day cure period under §13.1.
- CDUs are most of Fubeix's purchases (Letter §2.3). Fubeix has open bids for late-2026 and 2027 projects priced at the old list prices, so the margin impact is real.
- Under DA §18.5, Draisath's silence or delay will not amount to a waiver of the deadline. Any waiver must be in writing and signed by Draisath.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Advise the client not to withhold or short-pay** invoices at the adjusted prices pending a resolution.
2. **Approach Draisath commercially.** The ask should be a signed written waiver or amendment under §18.5. Possible forms include:
   - grandfathering the old prices for the specific bids already submitted (with a project list);
   - phasing in the 9% increase; or
   - an agreed price concession as part of the consent package in Issue 1.
3. **Correct the record** in the next communication. We should not continue to assert that the §6.3 negotiation period has been triggered, since that position is not defensible and weakens our credibility on the consent request.
4. **Process fix going forward.** The client should diarize the 45-day window on receipt of every Price Adjustment Notice. Note that the window may already be partly used up by the time the notice arrives.

---

### Issue 3: The side letter's narrower definition of "Products" excludes RDHx and spare parts from the minimum commitment

**Where:** Side Letter dated March 2, 2026, §1.2, §2, §4.1; DA §1.1 ("Products"), §5.1, §5.3, §13.2, §18.4; Term Sheet §5.2.

**What the documents say:**
- DA §1.1 defines "Products" as the CDUs, RDHx and spare parts listed in Exhibit A. Under DA §5.1, "[a]ll purchases of Products" count toward the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment. Term Sheet §5.2 expressly agreed that CDUs, RDHx and spare parts would all count.
- Side Letter §2.1 reduces the commitment from $8,000,000 to **$6,000,000 per Contract Year**, from Contract Year 1 (§2.2).
- Side Letter §1.2 also defines "Products" as "**solely the coolant distribution unit models** listed in Exhibit A, Part 1." Side Letter §2.3 counts only purchases "of Products" toward the commitment.
- DA §18.4 provides that "any signed side letter referencing the Distribution Agreement" controls over the DA. The side letter references the DA and states that it "forms part of the Agreement" (§4.1).

**Why it matters:**
- Because the side letter prevails, **RDHx and spare-parts purchases no longer count** toward the commitment. The headline reduction from $8M to $6M is therefore much less valuable than it looks, and could even be worse than the original deal. Under the original terms, the full product mix counted toward $8M. Now Fubeix needs $6M of **CDUs alone**.
- If Fubeix falls short, Draisath may, within 90 days after the end of the Contract Year (i.e., by about April 14, 2027, for Year 1), either convert the appointment to non-exclusive or terminate on 60 days' notice (DA §§5.3, 13.2). The non-compete in §4.3 would continue to bind Fubeix even after conversion to non-exclusive, so Fubeix would bear the restriction without the benefit of exclusivity.
- **Broader risk.** The side letter's definition is not expressly limited to the minimum-commitment provisions. Draisath could argue that, because the side letter "forms part of the Agreement" and prevails, "Products" now means CDUs only for *all* purposes. On that reading, it would narrow Fubeix's exclusive appointment (§3.1), Draisath's exclusivity covenant (§4.1), the reserved-account referral fee (§4.2) and Draisath's warranty and indemnity coverage (§§10, 14) to CDUs.
  - Side Letter §4.2 ("[e]xcept as set out in this Side Letter, the Agreement remains unchanged") cuts against that reading, but does not eliminate it.
  - The reading is unattractive to Fubeix either way, and we should close it off.
- The 9% CDU price increase will marginally help Fubeix reach a dollar-value CDU-only commitment. That is a small offset, not a solution.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend the side letter** by a written instrument signed by both parties (Side Letter §5.2; DA §18.5). The amendment should delete §1.2, or replace it so that "Products" has the DA §1.1 meaning, with CDUs, RDHx and spare parts all counting toward the $6,000,000. The amendment should apply retroactively to Contract Year 1.
2. Pending the amendment, **seek Draisath's written confirmation** that RDHx and spare-parts purchases count for Contract Year 1. As a fallback, ask Draisath to waive its §13.2 rights for Contract Year 1.
3. **Run the numbers now**, since Contract Year 1 ends January 14, 2027 (see open questions).
4. Include this in the consent package (Issue 1).

---

### Issue 4: The non-compete is overbroad (worldwide; all thermal management products; 18-month tail)

**Where:** DA §4.3, §13.6 (survival), §1.1 ("Affiliate"); Term Sheet §4.3 (cited in the ledger as Term Sheet §4, Exclusivity).

**What the documents say:**
- DA §4.3 provides that during the Term **and for 18 months after**, Distributor shall not, "directly or indirectly, through any Affiliate or otherwise," distribute, market, sell, promote or solicit orders for "**any thermal management products** manufactured by any person other than Supplier, **anywhere in the world**." DA §13.6 makes §4.3 survive termination.
- Term Sheet §4.3 agreed that Distributor would not deal in "competing coolant distribution units, within the Territory only," during the term only. It expressly stated that "Distributor's other product lines are not restricted, including its distribution of third-party air-side cooling equipment."

**Why it matters:**
- The drafted covenant goes well beyond the agreed deal on three axes:
  - **product scope:** all thermal management products, not just competing CDUs;
  - **geography:** worldwide, not the five-state Territory; and
  - **duration:** an 18-month post-term tail that the term sheet did not include.
- Fubeix's recitals describe its business as marketing thermal management equipment generally (DA Recital B). If Fubeix continues to distribute third-party air-side cooling, it **may already be in breach** of §4.3 as written. That would expose Fubeix to a §13.1 termination notice with a 30-day cure period, which Fubeix could only cure by exiting that business.
- The "through any Affiliate" language creates exposure for the Ostrava group after closing (see Issue 1).
- **Enforceability.** Under New York law, courts review restrictive covenants for reasonableness. A covenant this broad relative to Draisath's legitimate interest (CDU exclusivity in the Territory) is vulnerable. However, outcomes are unpredictable:
  - a court may partially enforce the covenant, may decline to enforce it entirely, or may enforce it as written, given the commercial setting;
  - DA §18.7 (severability) contains no express reformation or blue-pencil language.

  Fubeix should not plan its business around an assumption that the clause is unenforceable.
- **Term sheet as leverage.** The term sheet is non-binding except for §§12–13. The DA contains no integration clause, but the term sheet's own non-binding language means it is unlikely to override DA §4.3. Its value is as strong evidence of the agreed commercial deal and as negotiating leverage. A mutual-mistake or reformation argument is possible but would be uphill.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend DA §4.3** to match Term Sheet §4.3:
   - limit the restriction to competing coolant distribution units;
   - limit it to the Territory;
   - limit it to the Term, deleting the 18-month tail or at most shortening it substantially; and
   - expressly carve out air-side cooling and Fubeix's other existing product lines.
2. **Carve out Affiliates.** The "through any Affiliate" reach should be removed, or at least should exclude Fubeix Industrial, Ostrava and their other subsidiaries acting independently of Fubeix.
3. Consider **tying the non-compete to exclusivity**, so that it falls away if Draisath converts the appointment to non-exclusive under §13.2(a).
4. Pursue this in the consent package. Draisath will want to know whether Ostrava's portfolio competes, so the topic will come up regardless.

---

### Issue 5: Automatic five-year renewal with a 15-day opt-out window

**Where:** DA §2.1, §2.2, §18.1; Term Sheet §2.2.

**What the documents say:**
- The Initial Term is three (3) years from the January 15, 2026 Effective Date, ending January 14, 2029 (DA §2.1).
- DA §2.2 provides that the agreement "will automatically renew for **successive five (5) year renewal terms**." Non-renewal notice must be given "during the fifteen (15) day period ending ninety (90) days before the expiration." Notice given outside that period "is of no effect."
- Ninety days before January 14, 2029 is October 16, 2028. The opt-out window therefore runs from approximately **October 1/2 to October 16, 2028**, depending on how the 15-day period is counted.
- Term Sheet §2.2 agreed only "one-year renewal terms by mutual written agreement," with neither party obliged to renew.

**Why it matters:**
- If Fubeix misses a narrow window two years from now, it is locked in until January 2034. During that period it would remain bound by the $6M minimum (and the CDU-only counting in Issue 3), the non-compete with its tail (Issue 4), the consent restrictions and Draisath's pricing rights.
- Draisath has the same right to opt out, so Fubeix gets no security of tenure in return.
- An early notice is as ineffective as a late one, so the client cannot simply send one now.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend DA §2.2** to match the term sheet: one-year renewals by mutual written agreement only. As a fallback, accept automatic one-year renewals with an opt-out at any time up to 90 days before expiry, rather than a 15-day window. Include this in the consent package.
2. **Diarize now**, regardless of the outcome:
   - a reminder in early September 2028;
   - a non-renewal decision point by late September 2028; and
   - delivery of the notice in a manner compliant with §18.1 between October 2 and October 16, 2028. Aim for the middle of the window, because notice is effective "on receipt."

---

## 4. Mutual NDA (no issue identified)

The Mutual NDA dated October 6, 2025 governed pre-signing discussions. It runs for two years (to October 2027), with survival provisions. It does not affect the issues above. Two minor practical points:

- The NDA treats the term sheet and the parties' discussions as confidential. This does not prevent us from using the term sheet with Draisath.
- If Fubeix's DA terms or Draisath pricing have been or will be shared with Ostrava in deal diligence, that disclosure falls under DA §12.1, which permits disclosure to employees, Affiliates and advisors. Ostrava is not an Affiliate until closing. The client should confirm what has been shared with the buyer and on what confidentiality terms.

---

## 5. Open points to confirm with the client / matters not resolvable from the documents

**Change of Control**
1. Has anyone at Fubeix or Fubeix Industrial discussed the Transaction with Draisath informally or obtained any indication of consent? Has Draisath responded to the September 21 letter?
2. Does the acquisition agreement make Draisath consent a closing condition or a covenant? What is the current closing timeline? Can it accommodate a consent process?
3. Do Ostrava Climate Holdings or its portfolio companies manufacture or distribute thermal management products anywhere in the world? (This is relevant to §4.3 through Affiliates.)

**Price increase**
4. When did Fubeix actually receive the July 1 Price Adjustment Notice, and in what form? Was any written objection sent before August 15, 2026, including by email? This includes anything by a salesperson. Its form would need checking against §18.1.
5. Has Fubeix paid, short-paid or disputed any invoices issued at the adjusted CDU prices since October 1?
6. Which open customer bids were priced at the old CDU list prices? What volumes and delivery dates do they involve? (This is needed to frame a grandfathering request.)
7. We should obtain a copy of the July 1 notice to confirm it complies with §6.2.

**Minimum commitment**
8. What are Fubeix's Contract Year 1 purchases to date, split between CDUs, RDHx and spare parts? What is the forecast to January 14, 2027? Will CDU-only purchases reach $6,000,000?
9. Do Draisath's quarterly statements under DA §5.2 and Side Letter §3 count only CDUs or all products? This would show how Draisath reads the side letter.
10. Did Fubeix intend or understand the side letter to narrow "Products"? Is there any negotiation correspondence showing the CDU-only definition was a drafting point Draisath raised?

**Non-compete**
11. Which third-party products does Fubeix currently distribute (air-side cooling and any other thermal lines), and where? Has Draisath raised any concern about these lines?

**Execution and documents**
12. All signature blocks in the folder copies (DA, Side Letter, Term Sheet) are blank. We need fully executed copies. In particular, DA §18.4 gives precedence only to a **signed** side letter. If the side letter was never countersigned, its precedence (and the $6M reduction) would both be in question.
13. We need Exhibit B, Part 3: the written list of reserved hyperscale accounts that Draisath delivered on or before the Effective Date.
14. Has there been any other amendment, waiver or side letter beyond the March 2, 2026 letter?

---

## 6. Recommended next steps (in order)

| # | Action | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Call with the client and M&A counsel to cover the open points on the Transaction, purchase data, invoices and other product lines | This week |
| 2 | Advise the client not to short-pay invoices at the adjusted CDU prices | Immediately |
| 3 | Send a formal §17.2 consent request to Draisath (per §18.1), together with a negotiation package covering: (a) a side-letter fix on "Products"; (b) narrowing §4.3 and an Affiliate carve-out; (c) amending §2.2 renewal; and (d) price relief for open bids | Within ~1 week, well ahead of the December closing |
| 4 | Fallback: obtain Draisath's written confirmation or waiver on Contract Year 1 minimum counting | Before January 14, 2027 |
| 5 | Diarize the renewal window (October 1/2–16, 2028) and the 45-day window for future price notices | Now |

Happy to draft the consent request and the term sheet for the amendment package once we have the client's answers on items 1–3 and 8 above.

**To:** [Supervising Partner]
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 4, 2026
**Re:** Fubeix Thermal Distribution, LLC / Draisath Cooling Technologies, Inc.: review of distribution arrangements and recommended next steps

---

## 1. Summary

Fubeix's arrangements with Draisath create four material problems for the client. In order of urgency:

1. **Change of Control consent.** The pending acquisition of Fubeix's parent by Ostrava Climate Holdings needs Draisath's prior written consent, and Draisath may refuse it in its sole discretion. The September 21 letter only gives notice. If closing happens without consent, as expected in December 2026, Draisath can terminate immediately. **This is the most time-critical item.**
2. **Minimum purchase commitment counting.** The side letter cut the commitment to $6,000,000 per Contract Year. However, it also redefines "Products" as CDUs only, so RDHx and spare-parts purchases likely no longer count. The first Contract Year ends January 14, 2027, and a shortfall exposes Fubeix to loss of exclusivity or termination.

The mutual NDA (D5) does not raise any issue that affects the client's position. It is discussed briefly in Section 4.

**Key background facts:**
- The Distribution Agreement (D1) is effective **January 15, 2026**.
- Its Initial Term is **three (3) years from that date**, ending January 14, 2029 (D1 §2.1).
- The Territory is NY, NJ, PA, CT and MA (D1 §1.1).
- D1 is governed by New York law (§18.2).
- Under the order-of-precedence clause, a signed side letter referencing the agreement controls over the agreement, which controls over its Exhibits (D1 §18.4).
- The side letter (D2) sets the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment at **$6,000,000 per Contract Year** (D2 §2.1).

One general caveat applies throughout. The term sheet (D4) is expressly non-binding except for §§12–13 (D4 §13.2). Where the executed agreement departs from the term sheet, Fubeix has no contractual right to the term-sheet position. The term sheet is useful as **negotiating leverage**: it shows what Draisath agreed to commercially. It does not override D1.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Change of Control. The parent acquisition requires Draisath's prior written consent, and none has been requested

**Where:**
- D1 §1.1 ("Change of Control"), §17.2 and §13.3.
- D3 (September 21, 2026 letter) §§1.1–1.4.
- D4 §10.2 (for context).

**What the documents say:**
- **Definition.** "Change of Control" includes an acquisition of more than 50% of the voting interests of any entity that directly or indirectly controls the Party (D1 §1.1(a)).
- **Treated as assignment.** Under §17.2, any Change of Control of Distributor, "including a change of control of any entity that directly or indirectly controls Distributor," is deemed an assignment.
- **Consent standard.** An assignment requires Supplier's prior written consent, which Supplier may grant or withhold "in its sole discretion." An assignment that breaches §17.2 is void.
- **Termination right.** Under §13.3, Draisath may terminate **immediately** by written notice if a Change of Control occurs without its prior written consent.
- **The transaction.** D3 §1.1 confirms that Ostrava Climate Holdings has signed a definitive agreement to acquire **all** of the equity of Fubeix Industrial Group, Inc., Fubeix's parent. Closing is expected in December 2026 (D3 §1.2). This falls squarely within the definition.

**Why it matters:**
- **Notice is not consent.** D3 §1.4 says the letter "satisfies any notice requirement under the Agreement with respect to the Transaction." The agreement imposes no notice requirement for a Fubeix change of control. It imposes a **prior written consent** requirement. The letter does not ask for consent, and nothing in the folder shows that Draisath has given it.
- **Facts the letter stresses do not change the analysis.** D3 §1.3 notes that Fubeix remains a wholly owned subsidiary and that management and operations are unchanged. These points do not take the deal outside §17.2, which expressly covers indirect changes of control.
- **Exposure on closing.** If the deal closes without consent, Draisath gets an immediate termination right with no cure period. That would end Fubeix's exclusivity in the Territory. The 18-month post-term non-compete would still apply (see Issue 3; D1 §13.6).
- **Leverage for Draisath.** Because consent is in Draisath's sole discretion, Draisath can use the request to extract concessions, for example on pricing, the commitment or the non-compete.
- **Possible misstatement.** The §1.4 language could be read as Fubeix taking the position that no consent is needed. We should correct that position before Draisath relies on it.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Send a formal consent request now.** It should come from Fubeix under D1 §18.1, ideally after an informal call with Draisath's commercial lead. It should expressly request Draisath's prior written consent under §17.2 to the Transaction. It should also seek a confirmation that Draisath will not exercise its §13.3 termination right as a result of the Transaction.
2. **Withdraw the notice position.** The request should clarify or withdraw the statement in D3 §1.4 that notice satisfies the Agreement.
3. **Make consent a closing condition.** Coordinate with Fubeix Industrial and its deal counsel so that Draisath consent is a condition to closing, or at least a covenant, in the Ostrava purchase agreement. Alternatively, closing should be timed so that it does not occur before consent is received.
4. **Prepare for counter-asks.** Fubeix should be ready for Draisath to ask for something in return. If Draisath reopens terms, we can raise our own asks at the same time (Issues 2–4).
5. **Get it in writing.** The consent should be signed by Draisath (D1 §18.5) and should cover the Transaction as described, including any pre-closing restructuring.

---

### Issue 2: Side letter's narrower definition of "Products" excludes RDHx and spare parts from the minimum commitment

**Where:**
- D2 §1.2 and §2.
- D1 §1.1 ("Products"), §5.1, §5.3, §13.2 and §18.4.
- D4 §5.2 (for context).

**What the documents say:**
- **D1 definition.** D1 §1.1 defines "Products" as the CDUs, RDHx **and** spare parts listed in Exhibit A. D1 §5.1 counts "all purchases of Products" toward the commitment.
- **D2 definition.** D2 §1.2 defines "Products" as "**solely the coolant distribution unit models** listed in Exhibit A, Part 1" (DCT-CDU 350, 800 and 1500). D2 §2.3 then counts "Purchases of Products" toward the reduced $6,000,000 commitment.
- **Scope of the redefinition.** The D2 definition is not limited to any particular section of the side letter.
- **Precedence.** D2 references the Agreement and is a signed side letter. Under D1 §18.4, it controls over D1 in the event of any conflict or inconsistency. D2 §4.1 also states that the side letter "forms part of the Agreement."
- **Term sheet position.** The term sheet stated expressly that CDUs, RDHx and spare parts would all count (D4 §5.2).

**Why it matters:**
- **RDHx and spare parts likely stop counting.** The most natural reading is that only CDU purchases now count toward the $6,000,000 commitment. Fubeix's RDHx and spare-parts spend would then be disregarded.
- **The reduction may be largely illusory.** The headline cut is from $8M to $6M. A $6M CDU-only target could be harder to meet than the original $8M all-products target, depending on Fubeix's product mix.
- **Wider spillover risk.** The definition is not expressly limited to the commitment. There is an argument that it narrows "Products" for other purposes too, such as the exclusive appointment in §3.1 or Supplier exclusivity in §4.1, though §4.2 of the side letter cuts against that. The ambiguity alone is undesirable.
- **Consequences of a shortfall.** Under D1 §5.3 and §13.2, Draisath may, by notice within 90 days after the end of the Contract Year, either convert Fubeix to non-exclusive or terminate on 60 days' notice.
- **Timing.** The first Contract Year ends **January 14, 2027**, so this exposure is close.
- **Interaction with Issue 1.** A shortfall would give Draisath a second exit route at the same time it is considering the Change of Control consent.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend the side letter.** Negotiate a short amendment to D2, signed by both parties (D2 §5.2; D1 §18.5), that:
   - deletes D2 §1.2, or replaces it with "Products" as defined in D1 §1.1; and
   - confirms that all CDU, RDHx and spare-parts purchases count toward the $6,000,000 commitment from January 15, 2026.
2. **Pair it with the consent request.** This amendment can be handled alongside the Change of Control consent request.
3. **Check year-to-date figures now.** Use Draisath's quarterly statements under D1 §5.2 and D2 §3. If those statements already count only CDUs, that confirms Draisath's reading.
4. **Fall-back.** If Draisath resists, ask for a written waiver of any first-year shortfall, or a commitment that counts RDHx and spare parts.

### Issue 3: Non-compete is far broader than the term sheet, covering all thermal products, worldwide and post-term

**Where:**
- D1 §4.3 and §13.6 (survival).
- D4 §4.3.

**What the documents say:**
- **Executed restriction.** D1 §4.3 bars Fubeix, "directly or indirectly, through any Affiliate or otherwise," from distributing, marketing, selling, promoting or soliciting orders for "**any thermal management products** manufactured by any person other than Supplier, **anywhere in the world**."
- **Duration.** It applies during the Term and for 18 months after expiration or termination, and §13.6 confirms that it survives.
- **Term sheet restriction.** The term sheet covered only "competing coolant distribution units, within the Territory only," during the term. It stated expressly that Fubeix's other product lines, "including its distribution of third-party air-side cooling equipment," would not be restricted (D4 §4.3).

**Why it matters:**
- **It catches existing business.** On its face, §4.3 captures Fubeix's existing third-party air-side cooling business. That business is outside the deal Fubeix agreed, and Fubeix may already be in technical breach. If so, Draisath could cite that breach as a ground to terminate under §13.1, subject to the 30-day cure period.
- **The Affiliate language widens it.** The restriction extends to activity "through any Affiliate." After closing, Ostrava and its group will be Affiliates of Fubeix. If any Ostrava company distributes non-Draisath thermal products anywhere, Fubeix's exposure could expand. This should be raised with deal counsel.
- **The tail is long.** The 18-month post-term restriction would apply however the agreement ends, including after a Draisath termination under §13.2 or §13.3. It would restrict Fubeix's core business well after the relationship is over.
- **Enforceability does not rescue Fubeix.** Under New York law, a covenant this broad is vulnerable. The outcome is unpredictable, however: a court may partially enforce it rather than strike it, and D1 §18.7 preserves the rest of the agreement. Fubeix should not plan its business on the assumption that the clause will fail.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend D1 §4.3 to match the term sheet:**
   - limit the product scope to CDUs that compete with the CDUs listed in Exhibit A, Part 1;
   - limit the geography to the Territory;
   - limit the duration to the Term, deleting the 18-month tail or, as a fall-back, shortening it substantially and applying it only to CDUs in the Territory;
   - add a carve-out confirming that third-party air-side cooling and Fubeix's other existing lines are not restricted.
2. **Deal with the Affiliate wording.** Delete "through any Affiliate," or limit it to Affiliates acting on Fubeix's behalf, so that Ostrava-group businesses are not caught.
3. **Seek protection for the past.** Ask Draisath to confirm that it will not assert a breach based on Fubeix's existing activities.
4. **Use the term sheet and the consent request.** Use D4 §4.3 as the anchor in negotiation, and raise this point with the consent request.

### Issue 4: Automatic five-year renewal with a 15-day opt-out window

**Where:**
- D1 §2.1 and §2.2.
- D4 §2.2.

**What the documents say:**
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term runs three (3) years from January 15, 2026, ending January 14, 2029 (D1 §2.1).
- **Renewal.** D1 §2.2 provides that the agreement "will automatically renew for **successive five (5) year renewal terms**." Non-renewal notice is effective only if given during the 15-day period ending 90 days before expiry. Notice given outside that period "is of no effect."
- **Opt-out window.** For the Initial Term, the window runs from about **October 1 to October 16, 2028**.
- **Term sheet position.** The term sheet agreed to one-year renewals by mutual written agreement, with neither party obliged to renew (D4 §2.2).

**Why it matters:**
- **Risk of a five-year lock-in.** If Fubeix misses a 15-day window, it is locked in for a further five years. That would carry:
  - the minimum purchase commitment;
  - the overbroad non-compete, plus its 18-month tail; and
  - Draisath's pricing rights.
- **Notice outside the window fails.** A notice sent early or late is void, so precise diarization is essential.
- **Poor fit with the transaction.** The provision may not suit Fubeix's plans under new ownership.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend D1 §2.2 to match the term sheet.** The preferred position is one-year renewals by mutual written agreement.
2. **Fall-back.** If that is not achievable, accept:
   - one-year automatic renewals, with Fubeix able to give non-renewal notice at any time up to 90 days before expiry; and
   - no "of no effect" language for early notices.
3. **Diarize now.** Whatever happens in negotiation, the client and our docket should diarize the **October 1–16, 2028** window, with reminders well in advance. Fubeix should also confirm who internally owns this decision.
